subject.title: feat(talk): describe_view inline vision for OpenAI Realtime + Gemini Live

question: Should OpenClaw accept this browser-direct Video Talk `describe_view` boundary now, and if so how narrowly should same-origin camera permission be scoped?
rationale: The PR changes a camera permission boundary and sends user camera frames directly from browser to providers; automation can identify the risks, but maintainer security/product intent decides whether this capability belongs in core and which permission boundary is acceptable.

options.title: Scope And Prove Browser-Direct MVP
options.body: Keep `camera=()` as the shared Gateway default, add a narrow Control UI-only camera permission path, fix provider denial behavior, rebase onto current main, and require redacted real browser/provider proof before merge.

options.title: Accept Global Same-Origin Camera Policy
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally allow `camera=(self)` for all default Gateway responses only after explicit security review owns that broader boundary.

options.title: Pause For Transport Contract
options.body: Pause this PR and let the broader provider/gateway video-frame transport design at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89131 settle first.

recommendation.title: Scope And Prove Browser-Direct MVP
recommendation.body: Keep `camera=()` as the shared Gateway default, add a narrow Control UI-only camera permission path, fix provider denial behavior, rebase onto current main, and require redacted real browser/provider proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned on the live PR and has the strongest current-main history in the affected Talk UI/provider paths.
